verses.1: The people who walked in the darkness saw a great light. It was a light that came from those who lived in the land of shadow. It was a light that shone upon them.
verses.2: The people became very happy. They were joyful before you, just as they would be during the harvest time when they find their crops.
verses.3: For he has lifted up his burden and his staff; it is like the branch that is struck by the wind.
verses.4: For every sound, there is noise and chaos; it becomes a place of destruction and burning.
verses.5: For a son was born to us; a son was given to us. And the midwife took care of him. His name was Peleo. He warned our father, the king, about the coming disaster.
verses.6: For the sake of peace and justice, there is no limit to the time that David’s throne will remain in power. May his queen be able to reign with justice and righteousness from now until forever. The jealousy of Jehovah’s army will ensure that this happens.
verses.7: What Adonai sent to Jacob, and it fell upon Israel.
verses.8: And all the people shall know that Ephraim and Jerusalem are in a state of glory and greatness.
verses.9: To the trees, stones fell; and trees were built, but they withered away.
verses.10: And Jehovah will turn over the enemies of Rezin against them, and their troubles will be resolved.
verses.11: Aram from the east and Philistines from the west ate up Israel in every place. They did not stop until they had consumed everything. Their hands were still moving around, as if they still had energy left.
verses.12: And the people did not return to those who had defeated them, nor did they seek out Jehovah’s army.
verses.13: And Jehovah remembered Israel’s head and tail, as well as their bodies on that single day.
verses.14: The old and ugly one is the leader; the false prophet is the one who deceives others.
verses.15: And those people became foolish and their words were taken away from them.
verses.16: Therefore, they will not be happy on their holidays. Their gods and idols will not be merciful to them. All of their actions are evil and deceitful. In all this, they will not repent, and their hands will remain stubborn.
verses.17: For in the forest, like fire, evil deeds will be destroyed. It will be consumed and burned up in the depths of the forest. The smoke from it will fill the air.
verses.18: In the midst of Jehovah’s armies, the earth was devastated. The people became like a furnace of fire; each person was separated from his brother, and they could not be reconciled with each other.
verses.19: And he divided it into two parts. He ate on Mount Sinai. No one else was able to eat from that portion.
verses.20: Menas and Ephraim together destroyed Judah in all these ways. But their hands were still raised, and they continued to fight.
